messages:
jessie_support: FYI got a high-severity ticket from ACME — they're seeing a cascade of 429s on our dedicated pool after migrating plans. Says it started ~09:10 UTC and hasn't recovered.
jamal_oncall: I can take a look. Any customer request IDs or sample headers? 429s usually show the rate key in `x-rate-key` header.
jessie_support: Pasted logs from their request:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-key: tenant:acme-123:dedicated-pool-12
x-rate-units: 1000
x-rate-unit-period: minute
Retry-After: 30
```
They reported latency spikes right before the 429s. No other tenants reporting yet.
maria_infra: Hmm x-rate-unit-period=minute — our dedicated rate translator expects per-second units for the reserved pools. If the quota was ingested as per-minute, the slot allocator might be underestimating requests/sec and not scaling correctly. Can you share how the quota was created?
jessie_support: They self-serve migrated plan via billing portal last night. I pulled the tenant quota from the billing import job:
```
{ "tenant_id": "acme-123", "quota": { "units": 60000, "period": "minute" } }
```
Looks like the billing export used minutes (60000/min = 1000/s) but our ingester mapped "period" => denom incorrectly and set the runtime to `1000 units / second`? Not sure.
jamal_oncall: If the ingest mapping is wrong we could get two failure modes: 1) large unit count causes the rate limiter to think more capacity exists so it shouldn't 429 — but you said they're seeing 429s, so maybe it was interpreted the other way (divided to seconds wrongly) or the per-tenant cool-down logic is misfiring.
alex_eng: Quick note: dedicated pool autoscaler looks at token consumption per-second over a 30s sliding window. If the quota import sets a huge per-minute bucket but our token-bucket mapper divides by 60 (to seconds) and then clamps incorrectly, we can create an artificially low burst cap. I'll check the translator code path.
henry_billing: The billing->quota pipeline had a config change in last deploy: mapping.period_to_denom had a default fallback to "hours" when missing. I pushed a hotfix but we should verify any tenants that used explicit "minute" strings.
sre_bot: alert: dedicated-pool-12 evictions spike 09:11:03 -> 09:14:20 (noisy-neighbor-evict count: 14)
jessie_support: Repro steps ACME gave: 1) Send 10 parallel chat completions with seq len ~384, 2) wait 100ms, repeat 3x -> they hit 429s consistently. They shared a curl example:
```
for i in {1..10}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & done; wait
```
They also attached a sample trace id: trace-acme-2026-03-09-0912
jamal_oncall: I pulled traces for trace-acme-2026-03-09-0912 — saw queueing in the request router at pool ingress then immediate 429s. Router log: `quota_check: deny tenant acme-123 tokens=16 allowed=0`. So the runtime thought they had 0 available capacity.
maria_infra: Inspecting the quota DB for acme-123 shows two entries (legacy import + new billing import). One is per-minute 60000, other is per-second 1000 but with lower precedence. We merge entries by tenant id but our merge order was reversed after the deploy yesterday so the lower limit won. That's a bug.
alex_eng: That explains it. Merge logic change + period mapping risked producing an unintended per-second ceiling at 1000/s that then got clamped by our per-tenant cooldown to much lower effective rate. Proposed immediate mitigation: bump the tenant to a safe override in runtime (manual quota override) and roll back the billing-import merge order.
jessie_support: ACME on the line — can we do an immediate manual override? They need traffic back within 10 minutes.
jamal_oncall: I can apply a temp quota override on dedicated-pool-12 for tenant acme-123: set `override_quota=burst:2000, sustained:500` for 30 minutes. Doing now.
sre_bot: action_log: applied override override_id=ovr-9921 tenant=acme-123 pool=dedicated-pool-12 by=jamal_oncall at=1767777795
jessie_support: ACME confirms traffic is flowing again, latency back to normal. They're still worried about recurring issue.
maria_infra: Root cause steps: 1) billing import produced per-minute quota, 2) new mapper attempted to normalize to per-second but merge order with existing legacy record produced a lower-per-second record, 3) runtime honored merged lower limit causing unexpected throttling. Fix plan: revert the merge-order change in import job, add a unit-normalization test and a hard assertion that quotas are merged by source priority not timestamp. Also add detection alert if a tenant has >1 active quota record.
alex_eng: I'll open an eng PR for the importer + add a unit test for minute->second conversion + add a small monitor that flags tenants where merged_quota/unmerged_quota ratio > 10x.
henry_billing: I'll audit last 24h of billing imports and produce a list of affected tenants. If any high-spend tenants show up we'll coordinate outreach.
jamal_oncall: Post-mortem action items: (1) short-term: keep override for 30m then revert once importer fix deployed; (2) medium-term: change importer to collapse duplicates and enforce explicit unit denom; (3) add alert rule "quota-duplicate-detected" to support channel; (4) add an e2e repro test to CI using the curl pattern above.
jessie_support: Thanks team. I'll update the customer and mark ticket escalated->resolved after deploy. :white_check_mark:
alex_eng: I'll start the importer PR now and tag maria_infra for review.
maria_infra: ACK. I'll schedule the alert and run the billing audit after lunch. 👍
